build: Release Swift variants sharing the same verified Release Kotlin framework; separate full Release simulator build for visual review
metricNotes: CPU is app-process CPU time across threads, not utilization.
List readiness is a hierarchy check, not completed rendering.
CADisplayLink gaps are not Instruments rendering-hitch durations.
Inclusive trace CPU categories and rendering contexts overlap.
RSS values are checkpoints, not peak or long-session measurements.
Initial sweep has one process per workload; retained comparisons have three per variant.
Simulator measurements are not used for performance claims.
Wall-clock timestamps and run IDs are removed; all data is synthetic.

decisions.kept: Activity UITableView rendering the shared presentation snapshot; stable row/date IDs, reconfiguration and automatic sizing; existing search, navigation and Store5 observation.
reverted: Equatable SwiftUI Activity rows: scrolling CPU remained around 1.92 seconds versus 1.96 seconds baseline, with 34–37 ms callback gaps.
excluded: Initial table pilot before label compression and explicit large-title checks; not used in retained performance comparisons.
visualNotes: UIKit drawHierarchy fixture snapshots omitted some navigation content. A live iOS 18.6 simulator capture verified the visible title/search field and populated rows.
Full-tree XCTest interaction on the 7,500-row simulator list timed out; physical fixture search/navigation checks use public UIKit controls and delegates.
